Draw connecting lines between the constituent plans themselves, not just to the centre, to show they constrain each other. The interconnection is the point: this is integration, not collation. |
| 19 | 19.2 | `lo19-estimating-methods` | Top-down and bottom-up estimating methods | ### Estimation (19a) | Two groups. Top-down: parametric and analogous, marked as suited to the early life cycle when detail is scarce. Bottom-up: analytical and Delphi, marked as validating top-down once detail exists. Show a confidence axis increasing as methods are combined — a single method giving a wide cost-and-time spread, combined methods narrowing it. The narrowing spread is the argument for combining techniques. |
| 19 | 19.3 | `lo19-dependency-types` | Dependency link types | ### Dependency management (19a) | Three paired task bars showing the link types: finish-to-start (task 2 starts only when task 1 finishes), start-to-start (task 4 starts only when task 3 has started), finish-to-finish (task 6 finishes only when task 5 has finished). Label each link with its constraint in plain words. Keep it visually simple — this is a reference diagram learners will come back to when studying LO20. |
| 19 | 19.4 | `lo19-risk-structure` | Describing a risk as cause, event and impact | ### Risk identification (19a) | A three-part horizontal structure: cause (underlying circumstances) → uncertain event, shown with a probability marker → impact on project objectives, shown with an extent-of-effect marker. Use the worked example beneath it — general election, rising inflation, resource costs increase. Show that the same structure describes both a threat (downside impact) and an opportunity (upside impact), since that dual use carries into LO23. |

## Reconciling diagrams you have drawn

Two directions to check whenever a batch of artwork arrives:

1. **Artwork matches a placeholder** — set that diagram's `file` to the asset path in the LO
   JSON, then regenerate this register. The row moves from Awaiting artwork to Supplied.
2. **Artwork has no placeholder** — decide which LO and which body heading it belongs under, add a
   diagram object there with `id`, `figure_number`, `caption`, `placement`, `heading`,
   `file`, `alt`, and renumber that LO's figures in reading order.

A placeholder that will not be drawn should be deleted from the LO JSON, not left sitting in this
list — the body content it supports may need a table instead.
